source_anchor.prior_frontier: repair or recover the GitHub-hosted runner/account prerequisite responsible for zero-runner assignments and independently recover the Buildkite failing step

failure_pattern_attacked: The existing multi-job workflow could not prove whether repository validation structure contributed to failure because every job failed before steps. A minimal workflow with no checkout and one shell step was needed to isolate provider runner allocation.

durable_changes.purpose: minimal GitHub-hosted ubuntu-latest allocation probe with no checkout or repository validation dependency

falsification.result: Failure reproduces on a one-step ubuntu-latest workflow and again on provider rerun without any repository checkout or validation command executing.

claim_boundary: This proves persistence and independence from repository validation logic; it does not by itself identify the hidden GitHub account/billing/runner-policy prerequisite because the provider does not expose the pre-run annotation through the connected surface.

objective_state_delta.before: Runner-zero evidence came from the repository's normal eight-job validation workflow.
objective_state_delta.after: A dedicated minimal provider allocation probe now exists on main and independently reproduces the same pre-step failure twice, eliminating checkout, action version, and repository test logic as necessary causes of the GitHub Actions failure.

next_executable_frontier: Use repository/account administration or billing/provider support surface to inspect GitHub Actions execution eligibility for this private repository; separately recover Buildkite's failing step. Do not weaken repository validation or remove provider/host separation.
